_meta.description: Reference (literature) values for pure SU(2) lattice gauge theory with the Wilson plaquette action, used only for COMPARISON with this project's Monte Carlo results. None of these numbers is used as an input to any simulation.

conventions.a_sqrt_sigma: square root of the string tension in lattice units, a*sqrt(sigma). In the cited papers sigma is extracted from the mass of a flux loop (torelon) winding a spatial circle of length L (Polyakov-loop correlators) including the leading universal string correction, a*m_P(L) = a^2 sigma L - pi (D-2)/(6 L) [form of the correction quoted from memory; check the cited equation].
conventions.a_m_0pp: mass of the lightest scalar (0++) glueball in lattice units.
conventions.beta_c: critical coupling of the finite-temperature deconfinement transition on N_t x N_s^3 lattices, extrapolated to N_s -> infinity.

_meta.schema: Every leaf entry has: value, uncertainty (one standard deviation, same units as value; null if the source gives none), source, web_verified (boolean), verification_level, note. Optional 'alternatives' is a list of entries with the same fields.

verification_levels.search_excerpt: The number was read during a session on 2026-11-11 in a web-search result that quoted the cited source (typically the arXiv HTML/PDF text of the paper, or a later paper that cites it; the note says which). The full text itself could NOT be opened: direct access to arxiv.org, inspirehep.net and other hosts is blocked by the network policy of the session. Treat as 'seen in a quoted excerpt', which is weaker than 'checked against the published table'.
verification_levels.none: Not found during this session. Quoted from memory (the orchestrator's and/or the document author's). Must be re-checked against the cited paper before it is used for any quantitative claim.

_meta.warning: web_verified=true means verification_level=search_excerpt, NOT a line-by-line check of the published table. Numbers flagged 'from memory' may be wrong in the last digits and their uncertainties are rough estimates.

fact_check.who: Second, independent pass over this file on 2026-11-11 (adversarial fact-check). Same limitation as the first pass: only web search worked, no full text could be opened.

internal_consistency_checks.D4_Tc_over_sqrt_sigma: a*sqrt(sigma) interpolated log-linearly in beta to beta_c(N_t) gives T_c/sqrt(sigma) = 1/(N_t a sqrt(sigma)) = 0.676 (N_t=4, beta_c=2.2986), 0.686 (N_t=6, 2.4265), 0.698 (N_t=8, 2.510363) with the primary values, and 0.676, 0.691, 0.708 with the 16^4-row alternatives. Roughly constant, consistent with the literature 0.69-0.71 within the few-percent accuracy of this interpolation; the N_t=4 point is 2-4 percent low, which may be an O(a^2) effect or reflect that the beta=2.3 string tension comes from a small 10^4 lattice. Not a precision test.
internal_consistency_checks.D3_m0pp_over_sqrt_sigma: 1.19/0.2538 = 4.69, 0.765/0.1616 = 4.73, 0.559/0.1179 = 4.74: inside 4.6-4.8. Note that the three masses are from memory, so this checks only that the remembered numbers are mutually plausible.
internal_consistency_checks.D3_sqrt_sigma_over_g2: beta*a*sqrt(sigma)/4 = 0.3807, 0.3636, 0.3537 at beta = 6, 9, 12: decreasing towards the continuum 0.3353(18). A naive extrapolation in the bare 1/beta gives 0.327 (linear) or 0.319 (quadratic through the three points), i.e. 2-5 percent below 0.3353; the published value uses a different (improved-coupling) extrapolation and more beta values, so only the direction and rough size of the drift are tested here.

continuum_sqrt_sigma_over_g2.source: M. Teper, Phys. Rev. D59 (1999) 014512, arXiv:hep-lat/9804008, eq. (38) (continuum limit for SU(2)).
continuum_sqrt_sigma_over_g2.note: g^2 has dimension of mass in D=3 and is defined through beta = 4/(a g^2), so sqrt(sigma)/g^2 = lim_{beta->inf} beta*a*sqrt(sigma)/4. The excerpt quotes 0.3375(130) as 'consistent with the value of 0.3353(18) in eqn(38)'. Cross-check from another excerpt: Teper's fit sqrt(sigma)/g^2 = 0.1974(12) N - 0.120(8)/N (arXiv:hep-lat/9711011) gives 0.3348 at N=2. Warning: at beta = 6, 9, 12 the naive ratio beta*a*sqrt(sigma)/4 is 0.381, 0.364, 0.354, i.e. still 5-14 percent above the continuum value; Teper extrapolates with a mean-field improved coupling (statement about the improved coupling is from memory).
